reviews.comment: Dr. Sottile is a sweet and caring professor. I felt very motivated in his class and felt he was very talented. However, it was hard to keep up with his lectures. The class not only was incredibly fast-paced but the content felt exceedingly more difficult than it needed to be. Nonetheless, I enjoyed the class and do not regret taking it.
Great teacher. He gives out eggplants, watermelons, and donuts in classes.

Lectures offered nothing that the textbook didn't. Spent 1/3 of the class stuttering, 1/3 correcting his mistakes, and the last third yapping about theory that he never asks about on the exam. Apparently I was supposed to come into the class knowing the material... also makes the homework assignments extra tedious and difficult.
He is a very sweet person.

Frank is a genius, smart, and respected in the math department at TAMU but he is a terrible teacher. So many of his lectures would be difficult to follow as students are trying to keep up just for him to say "you wont be tested on this" He assigns so much homework and they are insanely hard. This class was not supposed to be as hard as he made it.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Sottile is an amazing lecturer. He teaches in a way that is both straightforward and easy to understand. However, he was a JERK. He (and his teaching assistants) would take points off for the smallest things. Also, he changed our final essay from 2500 words to 3000 words the day before it was due without telling anyone.

This is the hardest class I have ever taken. So much homework, lectures make no sense. If you take this class, the videos will help you more than anything else. He's a nice guy who is very passionate about math, but makes this class so much harder than it needs to be.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Sottile is very knowledgeable about math. He has high expectations for his students. Sometimes his lectures were hard to follow but ultimately if you use the book and take notes you'll probably be ok. Math 300 is tough but Sottile is a fine choice.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: His lectures are a mess despite having read the book before class, he made no sense, he talks in circles and contradicts himself constantly. When a student asks a question he finds the rudest way to respond back to them without answering the question to begin with. He doesn't seem to be happy with anything you do and doesn't know what he wants
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Frank (he tells us to call him by his first name) is just a great guy. He will help anyone who asks and is there for his students. He occasionally gets off topic but this is oftentime the result of off topic students. He expects you work hard and if you do he will reward you with a high grade. One of the nicest professors I have ever had.

I  am a student of University of Ibadan, Nigeria I was fortunate to be in professor frank sottile's class when he came as a visiting lecturer He was taking us something on higher dimension .Everything scattered at a point but he explained again and we got it. He is funny and fast .Trust me if you don't follow what he is doing  you are down there!

Prof Sottile is a great professor, you can go to his office hours and he will be there. His tests are extremely challenging and he knows it, but he works with the class on this. If you put the effort in and learn the material you will do well. He works well with students with disabilities which was really great. The homework is challenging but fun.
He's a nice guy and very enthusiastic about math, but he's really scatterbrained and hard to understand

Was in 151 Honors course.  I guess they figured that since we were honors students, we could deal with a terrible teacher.  Impossible to follow what he's doing.  Would also show us how to do a problem in class but would deduct points off of our tests if we worked the problem like him.
